youtubeTitle: The Gospel and Soul Health Session 8 - Dr Bruce Wauchope
chapter: 8th Non-negotiable: The loving relationship we have in Jesus with the Father, Son and Spirit is displayed in the "New Covenant"
summary: Bruce reviews the non-negotiables and adds the eighth: our loving relationship in Jesus with the Father, Son and Spirit is expressed in the New Covenant of Jeremiah 31 and Hebrews 8. Christ's objective work runs backwards and forwards through all history, but we live in our own time through this covenant. It has three clauses: God's laws written on our hearts and minds (Christ in us); no one teaching his neighbour 'know the Lord', which removes vertical spiritual authority and spiritual abuse; and God's mercy that does not remember sins. The covenant was cut in blood through our own violence in killing Jesus, which brings us back to the pre-creation purpose, and atonement means 'at-one-ment'. Bruce closes by showing what is lost when each non-negotiable is dropped: Molech, morality, anxiety, self-made religion, the hamster wheel and spiritual control.
keyPoints: Review: the Trinity's love and union; the pre-creation purpose; all in and through the eternal Son; made and sustained by him; his full entry into our darkness; whatever happened to him happened to us; and it is up to them, not plan B.
Christ's objective work runs backwards, forwards and sideways through history. In our own space and time, we live by the New Covenant.
Clause 1: 'I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts; I will be their God and they my people.' This prophesies Christ in us.
Clause 2: 'No one shall teach his neighbour, saying, Know the Lord, for all shall know me.' Guidance begins on the inside, and others confirm rather than lead.

This removes vertical spiritual authority. Apostles, prophets, pastors, teachers and evangelists come alongside to build people up in Christ; they are not above them. Kept, the covenant removes spiritual abuse.
Clause 3: 'I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins I will remember no more.' There is no plasma screen of your sins at death.
The story of a young girl in France: asked by a sceptical cardinal to find out his last confession, Jesus replied, 'I don't remember.' Words of knowledge should reveal who we are, not expose sin.
The goal is not getting our ledger right but our ontology: knowing who we are and living out of the Trinity's love (Paul Young, Wesley Chambers).
Institutional religion can act like the vampire Babylon of Revelation, sucking life from people through false meaning, guilt and fear, much like Molech.
No covenant is cut without blood. We cut this covenant through our violence in killing Jesus, and his blood brings us back to the pre-creation purpose. Atonement is 'at-one-ment'.
Lose any non-negotiable and you fall into error: Molech replacing the Father, anxious morality, a tangled Bible, a self-existent 'robot', self-made religion, or the hamster wheel.

When the gospel enters an institution it devolves it, from a 'performing seal' leader to elders to 'the people of the church'. The outcome is guaranteed by the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.

keyTerms.definition: God's covenant (Jeremiah 31, Hebrews 8) by which we live our relationship with the Trinity in our own time.
Christ himself within us, so that guidance comes from inside.
One person claiming spiritual rule over another, which the New Covenant removes.
Control of people through claimed spiritual authority, guilt or fear.
Focus on a legal record of sins, as opposed to knowing who we are in Christ.
Atonement understood as God and humanity made one, dwelling in each other through Christ.
Christ's blood, shed by our violence, through which the covenant was cut.

quotes: No pastor, no evangelist, no priest, no prophet has authority over you in Christ.
It's not about what you've done; it's about who you are.
Dad's especially fond of you, and especially fond of you. (Paul Young)

caseStudy.title: The controlling small-group leader
caseStudy.scenario: Ben, 26, joined a church where his small-group leader expects to approve major life decisions, including jobs, relationships and how much he gives. When Ben disagrees, he is told he is 'out of God's will' and reminded of past sins he once confessed. He feels anxious, watched and unable to trust his own sense of God's leading.
caseStudy.analysis: The New Covenant's second clause, 'no one shall teach his neighbour, Know the Lord', removes vertical spiritual authority, and the third clause means God doesn't use remembered sins against us. Ben is experiencing the kind of institutional control Bruce warns about. Christ is in Ben, and leaders are meant to come alongside him, not rule over him.
pathway: Read Jeremiah 31:31-34 and Hebrews 8:10-12, and note the three clauses.
Practise listening for Christ's leading within, then invite trusted friends to confirm rather than direct.
Calmly decline control ('That's nice for you'), without becoming controlling in return.
Refuse to let confessed sins be used against him, since God remembers them no more.
If the controlling behaviour continues, seek wise outside counsel; spiritual abuse can need professional support.

practices.name: Covenant on the fridge
practices.how: As Bruce suggests, write out the three clauses of Jeremiah 31:33-34 and put them where you'll read them every day.

practices.name: Inside-out discernment
practices.how: Before a decision, sit quietly with Christ in you first, then ask two friends to confirm, not decide.

practices.name: Ledger release
practices.how: Write down a past sin you keep replaying, read 'I will remember their sins no more' over it, and then destroy the paper.

reflection: Where have you handed spiritual authority over your life to someone else?
Do you relate to God more by 'ledger' or by 'ontology', by what you've done or who you are?
How might your community change if everyone believed 'all shall know me, from the least to the greatest'?

quiz.q: Which clause of the New Covenant removes vertical spiritual authority?
options: 'I will put my laws in their minds'
'No one shall teach his neighbour, saying, Know the Lord'
'I will remember their sins no more'
quiz.explain: Since everyone knows God from within, no one stands above another spiritually.

quiz.q: In the story Bruce tells, what did Jesus say about the cardinal's last confession?
quiz.explain: It illustrates 'their sins I will remember no more'.

quiz.q: How does Bruce say the covenant was 'cut'?
options: Through animal sacrifices in the temple
Through our violence in killing Jesus, whose blood is the blood of the covenant
quiz.explain: No covenant is cut without blood, and we shed his.
